newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU flour export tally up 200,000 T in past week.
newsitem.headline: EU flour export tally up 200,000 T in past week.

text.p: Flour export commitments rose by another 200,000 tonnes in the week running up to Thursday's European Union grain tender, where the Commission acted to discourage further sales for the time being, figures show.

Data distributed to the EU's cereals management committee in Brussels on Thursday showed flour export commitments between July 1 and March 4 stood at 5.036 million tonnes, compared with 4.819 million tonnes up to February 25.
The EU Commission moved in three stages this week to prevent a run on flour export licences after a wide gap opened up between wheat grain and flour export refunds.
First, it rejected export bids for 140,000 tonnes in its daily bidding channel at a standing refund of 17 Ecus per tonne.
Then on Wednesday it cut the refund to 10 Ecus per tonne to discourage further bidding.
Finally at the main grain tender on Thursday it cut the flour refund again to eight Ecus per tonne, where it is now below the 10.25 Ecu maximum refund last given for wheat.
An EU official described the new refund as a "non-operational" level designed to damp down the market while leaving some margin for those who really had to do business.
